newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dana Petroleum completes Siberian drilling.
newsitem.headline: Dana Petroleum completes Siberian drilling.

text.p: Irish exploration firm Dana Petroleum said on Tuesday that it had completed the drilling of a new oil production well in its South Vat-Yoganskoye field in western Siberia.
In a statement, chief executive Tom Cross said the well, which is centrally located in the field, was drilled to a total depth of over 2,300 metres (7,546 feet).
"Drilling took less than one month and was ahead of schedule and under budget," said Cross.
He said the well, which had been logged and cased, encountered a full reservoir section.

"All the expected sand units were present and proved to be thicker than anticipated. Following these encouraging results, the drilling rig has been kept on location and has already spudded a second well," he added.
Cross said that when drilling of this second well is completed, both wells would be flow tested to assess field productivity and tied into the export pipeline built earlier in 1996.
Dana Petroleum owns a 50 per cent stake in the Vat-Yoganskoye oilfield with the remainder held by a group of Russian oil companies including Lukoil, Russia's largest oil company.
